Fitch Ratings recently affirmed Turkiye's long-term issuer default ratings at 'BB minus' with a stable outlook.

Fitch projects inflation will fall from 32 per cent in June to 29.5 per cent at end-2026 and 18 per cent at end-2028, still the highest of any sovereign it rates.

title: June erased 85% of Pakistan’s $17.93 billion textile export gain
summary:
Pakistan’s textile exports rose just 0.26 per cent in FY2026, but June’s sharp volume-led decline erased most of the year’s gains. 
TexPro data show apparel and fabric exports had already weakened in key Western markets, while growth relied heavily on China-bound yarn. 
FY2027 will depend on whether July–August orders confirm a temporary disruption or a broader demand slowdown.

title: PFAS-free textiles: What manufacturers need to know in 2026
summary:
PFAS-free manufacturing is rapidly becoming a global textile standard as regulations tighten and brands strengthen chemical compliance. 
US state-level restrictions, safer water-repellent technologies, stricter testing, and digital traceability are reshaping sourcing and production. 
Early adopters can improve market access, reduce compliance risks, and strengthen long-term competitiveness.

title: Weak monsoon sends India's cotton sowing to multi-year low
summary:
India's cotton sowing fell 15.33 per cent year on year to 79.54 lakh hectares as of July 10 due to delayed and uneven monsoon rains, raising concerns over another weak crop.
The acreage is also well below the five-year average.
With 2025-26 production already at an eight-year low, a smaller crop could tighten domestic supplies and increase import dependence if mill demand remains firm.

title: India, Estonia strengthen digital economy partnership
summary:
India and Estonia agreed to expand digital governance, fintech, cybersecurity and emerging-technology cooperation during Piyush Goyal’s Europe visit.
Estonia backed early India-EU FTA implementation, relevant to textile and apparel exporters, importers and sourcing teams.
The wider tour advanced trade, investment and technology talks, including investment protection and geographical indications.

title: Indian polyester raw material prices rebound on stronger crude oil
summary:
Indian polyester raw material prices rebounded during the week as higher upstream feedstock costs lifted domestic prices.
PTA and melt prices increased, while MEG remained unchanged.
Polyester filament yarn producers also raised FDY, POY and PTY prices.
In China, PTA and MEG strengthened on firmer energy markets.
The near-term outlook remains firm, supported by global feedstock trends.

title: Vietnam's H1 export surge masks a looming US tariff shock
summary:
Vietnam’s H1 2026 gains came from shipment front-loading before the July 24 US tariff deadline, with Q1 apparel imports up 2.5 per cent to $4.02 billion. 
Replacing the 10 per cent Section 122 duty with a 12.5 per cent Section 301 tariff would add about $425 million in annual duties. 
Fabric (+20.7%) and fibre (+57.2%) imports surged as buyers built inventories ahead of the tariff reset.

title: Bangladesh factory closures trigger global sourcing shift
summary:
457 factories have closed since August 2024, including 155 in Gazipur, as gas shortages keep many units at 50-60 per cent capacity. 
January-May 2026: Bangladesh’s US exports fell 8.1 per cent, EU (-18.89%); Vietnam (+1.5%), Cambodia (+14.9%) and Indonesia (+5.5%) gained.
H&M is shifting part of its ~$5 billion Bangladesh sourcing to India, turning buyer diversification into active reallocation.

title: EU, euro area inflation ease in June: Eurostat
summary:
Euro area annual inflation eased to 2.8 per cent in June 2026 from 3.2 per cent in May, while European Union inflation fell to 2.9 per cent from 3.3 per cent, according to the Eurostat.
Inflation fell in 22 Member States, was stable in three and rose in two; Sweden, Czechia and Denmark had the lowest rates, with Romania highest at 9.2 per cent.

title: 54% of tested tops fail EU fibre checks in $68 bn trade
summary:
EU tests found incorrect fibre labelling on 37 per cent of garments, with blended fabrics showing the highest failure rates. 
TexPro data place the greatest commercial exposure in the $68.43 billion tops market. 
As Digital Product Passports and EPR rules advance, verified fibre data will become critical for compliance, recycling, traceability and market access.

title: UK study to examine microplastic impact of counterfeit football shirts
summary:
University of Portsmouth researchers are launching the first study into environmental impacts of counterfeit football shirts.
The UK Intellectual Property Office-funded work will compare authentic and fake kits for microplastic shedding, carbon impact and disposal.
Findings are intended to guide brands, policymakers and environmental groups on enforcement, consumer messaging and textile-waste.

title: UK clothing exports increase 9.5% in May 2026
summary:
The UK's clothing exports rose 9.54 per cent year on year to £264 million (~$356.62 million) in May 2026 and jumped 18.38 per cent from April.
However, Q1 2026 clothing exports fell 7.87 per cent year on year, while full-year 2025 exports declined 9.17 per cent, reflecting continued pressure despite the strong monthly rebound in May 2026.

title: Greece's apparel imports up 9.4% in Q1, led by cotton garments
summary:
Greece's apparel imports rose 9.36 per cent year on year to $654.31 million in Q1 2026, led by strong demand for cotton garments.
Spain remained the largest supplier, followed by Italy and Germany, while cotton apparel accounted for 46.58 per cent of total imports.
Greece's apparel imports have grown steadily, reaching $2.72 billion in 2025.

title: EU bans destruction of unsold clothes, footwear from July 19
summary:
From July 19, large EU companies cannot destroy unsold clothes, clothing accessories and footwear under ESPR rules.
Medium-sized firms will face the same obligations from 2030, while small and micro-businesses are exempt.
Brands, retailers and suppliers must prioritise resale, donation, repair or reuse, with records kept for five years for inspections.

title: Morocco’s $3.94 bn apparel boom hides a $900 mn textile gap
summary:
Morocco exported $3.94 billion of apparel in 2025 but imported $4.36 billion of yarn and fabric, exposing a structural upstream gap despite a strong garment surplus. 
Heavy reliance on imported materials and CMT manufacturing limits value capture. 
Future competitiveness will depend on integrated production, traceability, recycled materials and full-package manufacturing.

title: Bharat Tex 2026 backs global growth for Indian apparel brands
summary:
Indian textile and apparel brands discussed international scaling at Bharat Tex 2026, with export performance and 2030 targets framing the opportunity.
The session focused on converting manufacturing strength into design-led, culturally distinctive retail growth. 
Quality, sustainability, traceability, craft heritage and omnichannel reach emerged as priorities for global competitiveness.

title: UK's clothing imports drop 9.3% YoY in May 2026
summary:
The UK's clothing imports fell 9.3 per cent year on year to £1.301 billion (~$1.760 billion) in May 2026 and were 4.3 per cent lower than April, while textile fabric imports declined 2.8 per cent annually.
In Q1 2026, clothing imports eased 3.04 per cent year on year.
Despite the slowdown, the UK's clothing imports rose 6.05 per cent to £17.729 billion in 2025.

title: July's triple compliance shock hits apparel importers
summary:
CPSC eFiling adds an average $1,104 first-year compliance cost, affecting 43,000+ firms and 211,000+ children's product importers. 
The end of de minimis and USPS fees of up to $50 per non-compliant parcel raise fixed costs for low-value apparel shipments. 
Three July policy changes favour larger brands, widening their cost and operational advantage over smaller importers.

summary:
